entries.title: LabyrinthOS Current State
entries.summary: LabyrinthOS is a geospatial operating picture that persists source-attributed signals before higher-level interpretation.
entries.body: The product unifies global open-source, public, commercial, field, and physical data signals into a live operating picture. Current work must remain database-backed and source-attributed. Revalidate dated audit material against the configured integration branch before relying on it.

entries.title: LabyrinthOS System Architecture
entries.summary: The application separates signal ingestion and persistence from geospatial presentation and interpretation.
entries.body: Read the current architecture and ingestion contract before changing source adapters, storage, APIs, or map layers. Source adapters must preserve neutral records and provenance before interpretation.

entries.title: Signal Persistence Contract
entries.summary: Current signals, observation history, and imagery manifests have distinct persistence responsibilities.
entries.body: `signals` stores the latest snapshot per entity or event. `signal_observations` stores append-only history for playback and audit. `imagery_frames` stores time-indexed imagery manifests. Ingestion must persist neutral, source-attributed records before higher-level interpretation.

entries.title: Product and Interface Intent
entries.summary: Product and UI work must follow the guiding principles and tactical interface design system.
entries.body: Treat the product guidance and tactical design system as current requirements for product or UI work. Reconcile implementation proposals with both documents before approval.

entries.title: Worktree and Data Safety
entries.summary: Branch work belongs in managed worktrees; live database and runtime data must remain outside the repository.
entries.body: Treat `/Volumes/OPENFRONT/project-tempest` as the admin root. Perform branch work in a matching worktree. Keep PostgreSQL data, logs, PIDs, and ingest runtime artifacts under `/Volumes/OPENFRONT/project-tempest-data`, never in the repository or a worktree.

entries.title: LabyrinthOS Operating Workflow
entries.summary: Database, backup, and ingest commands must respect the external data and runtime boundaries.
entries.body: Confirm the correct worktree. Use the project database commands and take a backup before destructive database work. Start ingestion only after validating that data and runtime paths resolve outside the workspace.

entries.title: LabyrinthOS Open Questions
entries.summary: Curated unresolved product and engineering decisions awaiting explicit resolution.
entries.body: No baseline open question is promoted as current. Add questions here only through an approved documentation goal with source evidence and ownership.

entries.title: LabyrinthOS Historical Documentation Map
entries.summary: Dated architecture and branch notes remain useful evidence but require current-code verification.
entries.body: The architecture and engineering directories contain many dated plans, audits, and branch summaries. Search them for provenance, but do not treat a dated document as current unless a current memory entry or code review revalidates it.
